Wiki has a list of all Apollo astronauts and also lists if/when they died. It's actually 8 astronauts, not 7 as the article stated which further reduces the "abnormality." And when you look at the 3 that died we get:

  • Neil Armstrong
  • James Irwin
  • Ronald Evans

We can already remove Irwin from any sort of linked causality. He literally had a heart attack in space when in a high duress situation a preexisting undiagnosed condition showed up. We can also remove Armstrong who died at age 82 from blocked arteries as opposed to any sort of mysterious coronary disease. So that finally leaves exactly one astronaut out of 8 - which is already a number well within statistical margins (as it would be if you included Neil as well). And on top of this all there's 19 (!!) other Apollo astronauts in their 80s who have quite evidently not had mysterious terminal cardiovascular failure.
